title: Applied ML Eval Harness, Prompt Sets, Onboarding, Guardrails, Quantization, and Regression Triage — Unified Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's applied ML evaluation practices: the eval harness standards, prompt set and benchmark guidance, model onboarding checklist, quality guardrails, quantization profile expectations, and the regression triage playbook. It is intended as the canonical reference for ML Engineers, Applied ML, and Platform teams when bringing models into our serving pipeline or investigating regressions.

Scope

- Eval harness implementation and CI integration
- Prompt set authoring, storage, and benchmark run cadence
- Model onboarding: functional, performance, and safety gates
- Quality guardrails for serving and canarying
- Quantization profile creation and validation
- Regression detection, triage, and rollback procedures

Roles & Ownership

- Applied ML Team (owner): overall eval harness, prompt catalog, quality metrics.
- Serving Runtime (owner): performance bench & regression signals for latency/throughput.
- Platform/CI Team: test infra, reproducible runs, artifact storage.
- Security/Trust: safety-related prompt reviews and confidentiality gating.

Standards (high level)

1) Eval Harness

- The eval harness must be deterministic given a seed and recordable: commits that change harness code must include a changelog and unit tests.
- CI runs: every model onboarding PR triggers: unit test suite, smoke generation test (5 sample prompts), and a baseline eval: small prompt-set (50 examples) measuring POI metrics.
- Artifacts: raw model outputs, token-level timings, model config (weights, tokenizer version, quantization profile), and eval summary JSON must be uploaded to the artifact store with a stable run id.

2) Prompt Sets & Benchmarks

- Prompt sets are versioned and stored in the prompt catalog with metadata: name, intent, domain, median_length, label_schema, owner, and last_reviewed.
- Benchmarks are classified by purpose: functional (unit), behavioral (safety/guardrail), and cost/perf (latency, memory).
- Naming convention: <domain>-<intent>-<version> (e.g., docsqa-factual-v1).
- Bench runs cadence: nightly smoke runs for critical routes, weekly full runs for models in production, and on-demand runs for PRs or rollouts.

3) Model Onboarding Guide (high-level checklist)

- Pre-PR: write model card draft with scope, known limitations, and training data provenance.
- PR: include baseline eval harness results and comparison against current production model on defined prompt sets.
- Safety review: any model with open-web pretraining must pass safety checklist (toxicity, PII leakage tests).
- Performance gates: latency P50 must be within X% of target for the selected serving profile; throughput must sustain expected QPS for test batch.
- Regression plan: define canary config, rollback criteria, and monitoring dashboards.

Model Onboarding — Detailed Procedure

1. Create model card: include metadata (architecture, tokenizer, FLOPs estimate, quantization compatibility).
2. Add prompt sets: select 3 mandatory prompt sets: functional smoke (50), regression suite (500), safety suite (200).
3. Run eval harness: record outputs and compute metrics. Required metrics: accuracy (task-specific), calibration (where applicable), toxicity percentiles, perplexity on internal corpora, token latency distribution.
4. Quantization profiling (if applicable): run quant profiles (int8, int4 where supported) and collect MSE/RMSE of logits, and delta in downstream metrics.
5. Review and sign-off: Applied ML review, Security review (if safety flags), and Serving Runtime approval for performance.

Quality Guardrails

- Production SLOs (examples):
  - Generation latency: P50 < 150ms, P95 < 450ms for short responses (<=128 tokens) on dedicated serving profile.
  - Error rate (HTTP 5xx): < 0.2% over a 1h window.
  - Quality regressions: any drop > 3% absolute on primary metric vs baseline triggers triage.

- Guardrail checks in CI:
  - Safety-suite pass-rate >= 99% (no catastrophic safety failures).
  - Semantic quality delta <= allowed tolerance per model family.

- Canary policy template:
  - Canary size: 1-5% of traffic for 24h (non-critical), or 0.5-1% for critical flows.
  - Automated rollback triggers: latency P95 increase > 2x baseline, error rate > 1%, or quality metric drop > threshold defined in onboarding.

Quantization Profiles

- Profiles must be stored alongside model artifacts in the quantization registry with fields: profile_name, target_bits, calibration_dataset_id, representative_input_examples_count, score_delta_metrics.
- Validation steps:
  - Functional parity check: run regression suite; max allowed delta = 1.5% absolute (task dependent).
  - Logit-level drift: RMSE threshold (float32 vs quant) defined per model family (e.g., 0.02 for decoder-only LLMs).
  - Perf gain report: tokens/sec and memory reduction numbers.

Example quantization profile table (for onboarding doc):

| profile_name | bits | calib_dataset | rep_examples | max_metric_delta | owner |
|--------------|------|---------------|---------------|------------------|-------|
| rwi-int8-2026 | 8    | docsqa-v1     | 1024          | 1.0%             | Applied ML |
| rwi-int4-aggressive | 4 | conversational-v2 | 2048 | 2.5% | Applied ML |

Regression Triage Playbook

1) Detection

- Signals to monitor: nightly benchmark deltas, production alerting (quality SLO breaches), customer reported regressions, and A/B test failures.
- Priority levels: P0 (customer-impacting or catastrophic), P1 (significant quality or perf regression), P2 (minor model drift).

2) Initial Triage (15-30 minutes)

- Owner: on-call Applied ML or the last deployer of the model.
- Steps:
  1. Reproduce the regression locally against the recorded artifact and CI eval harness with the same seed.
  2. Check recent commits to eval harness, prompt sets, model weights, or quant profiles.
  3. Inspect monitoring dashboards: metric trend of primary metric, token latency distribution, and error rate.

3) Deep Triage (2-8 hours)

- Hypotheses to evaluate: model weights change (bad checkpoint), mismatch in tokenizer or preprocessor, quantization drift, prompt set skew, or eval harness bug.
- Run A/B between suspect revision and last-good artifact using the regression suite and a larger held-out set (>=5k examples if available).
- If safety-related regression, escalate to Security/Trust immediately and freeze rollout.

4) Mitigation and Rollback

- If reproduced and critical: initiate rollback to last-good artifact and open incident in incident response tracker.
- If root cause is fixable (e.g., eval harness bug), create a hotfix PR with tests, run full benchmarks, and coordinate redeploy.

Example incident checklist (short):

- Time detection: {{time}}
- Owner assigned: {{name}}
- Repro status: reproduced / not reproduced
- Immediate mitigations: rollback / throttle traffic / enable fallback model
- Communication: notify incident channel, affected customers (if any), and postmortem owner assigned

CI / Automation Requirements

- All eval harness runs must produce an artifact bundle including: run_id, git_sha, model_card_id, prompt_set_ids, quant_profile_id (optional), outputs.tar.gz, metrics.json.
- Artifact naming convention: eval-<model>-<run_date>-<shortsha>. Example: eval-rwi-llama2-20261115-4f2a9b.
- Nightly jobs: run production model against production-critical prompt sets and publish deltas to the alerting pipeline.

Example eval run metrics.json (trimmed)

{
  "run_id": "eval-rwi-llama2-20261115-4f2a9b",
  "model": "rwi-llama2-13b",
  "prompt_sets": ["docsqa-factual-v1", "safety-core-v2"],
  "metrics": {
    "docsqa_accuracy": 0.768,
    "toxicity_p95": 0.0012,
    "latency_p50_ms": 124
  }
}

Rollout & Canary Checklist

- Pre-rollout: confirm all required reviews, artifacts uploaded, and monitoring dashboards provisioned.
- Canary: start at 1% for 24h, evaluate automated signals and manual inspection at 6h and 24h.
- Scaling: increase to 10% for an additional 24-48h before full rollout.

Related Dashboards & Alerts (examples)

- ML-Evals-Nightly-Delta (alert on > 3% drop on primary metric)
- Model-Serving-Latency (alert on P95 > 2x baseline)
- Safety-Alerts (trigger on any failing safety-suite example)

Troubleshooting Examples (common failure modes)

- Symptom: sudden drop in factual accuracy after quantizing to int4.
  - Root cause check-list: verify quant profile used during serving matches the evaluated profile, compare logits RMSE, run int8 profile to compare degradation curve.

- Symptom: increased hallucinations post-deploy.
  - Root cause check-list: confirm prompt preprocessing pipeline unchanged, inspect tokenization differences, re-run eval harness with expanded safety & hallucination prompt sets.

FAQs

Q: When do we accept a model with >1% metric delta under quantization?
A: Exceptions require Applied ML and Product sign-off and automated fallbacks for critical flows; document the acceptance criteria in the model card.

Q: Who can trigger a rollback?
A: Any on-call applied-ml engineer or serving runtime SRE can execute an automated rollback when an alert meets the automated rollback criteria specified in this playbook.

Appendix: Example Prompt Set Metadata JSON (stored as a text artifact)

{
  "id": "docsqa-factual-v1",
  "domain": "docs-qa",
  "owner": "Applied ML",
  "size": 500,
  "labels": ["factuality", "long-context"],
  "last_reviewed": "2026-08-15"
}
